## Source findings and unresolved corrections

EGST88 is a survey with new application results. Its Theorem 7(a), rather than Theorem 6(a), is the explicitly stated Newman conclusion in the supplied copy. Its Subspace-Theorem deduction is explicitly a sketch, and the deep theorem is attributed to Schmidt/Schlickewei. Treating the entire finiteness input as an elementary consequence of coprimality would omit the essential mathematics. Theorem 6(a) requires pairwise coprimality and cannot simply be applied to arbitrary Newman summands; Theorem 7 supplies the additional argument.

The Tijdeman–Wang erratum explicitly declares the original Lemma 3(b) false and replaces the proof of Theorem 3. The replacement states that `3^b ∣ 2^a + 1` implies `a ≥ 3^(b-1)` in its intended positive-`b` setting, proved using the multiplicative order of 2 modulo powers of 3. For example, `3^4 ∣ 2^27 + 1` contradicts the original claimed constant bound on `b`; `original_tw_lemma_counterexample` checks this example in Lean. The corrected nonnegative solution list remains the eight tuples printed in the erratum, with one additional solution over integer exponents. If the explicit classification route is ever used, import the corrected proof, handle `b = 0` explicitly, and recheck every affected use, including the original paper's invocation of Lemma 3(b) inside Theorem 2. The code uses neither Lemma 3(b) nor the Theorem 2/3 classification arguments; M3.5 uses only Lemma 2, proved independently in Lean.

The preferred Theorem 5/6 route uses Lemma 6's projective S-unit finiteness and does not use Lemma 3(b), Theorem 3 or the explicit four-representation classification. Its positive rational summands cannot have vanishing subsums within one representation. Signed differences still can, and these require the full partition argument.

All three Bajpai–Bennett editions inspected agree on the displayed top-level bound 9 and thresholds 131082, 19700, 2316, 786 and 300 for their distinct-representation convention. The October manuscript changes `ω` to `w`; the thesis retains `ω`. Equation numbers change: v1's families (22)–(39) become manuscript (21)–(38), and the fully illustrated case changes from (28) to (27). The corresponding solution-count table retains the listed counts. The two manuscript dates and the thesis preface do not independently prove equality with the final Acta Arithmetica publication, cited by the Issue as volume 214 (2024), 421–458, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4064/aa230725-14-9). Final-published-version reconciliation remains unresolved and is not relied upon by the current qualitative route.

Verification checked the [publisher's article record](https://www.impan.pl/en/publishing-house/journals-and-series/acta-arithmetica/all/214/0/115468/effective-s-unit-equations-beyond-three-terms-newman-s-conjecture), confirming the authors, volume, pages, DOI and online publication date 21 February 2024. The available download link did not yield the final article PDF in this pass. Bibliographic confirmation is not final-text reconciliation, and the October 2023 manuscript remains identified as a manuscript.

The later route explicitly leaves analogous calculations available on request and references [Newman-data](https://www.math.ubc.ca/~bennett/Newman-data). Its computations include the 1431 primitive five-term solutions, continued-fraction inequalities, 64134 coefficient values, Maple ModularLog exclusions and remaining case searches. These are mathematical proof obligations, not trusted executable certificates obtained in this run. They have not been independently reconstructed or checked. No principal theorem in this project relies on them.

## M3.3 proved analytic component

`Analytic.lean` proves the actual normalized absolute-value/product hypotheses at places `∞,2,3`, using pinned Mathlib `padicNorm` with `|p|ₚ = p⁻¹`. Closure induction proves `threePlaceProduct u = 1` for every member of the fixed S-unit group and `padicNorm p u = 1` for primes outside 2 and 3. It proves positive three-place pair height, height at least 1 for our normalized relations, invariance under S-unit common scaling, and linear independence of either coordinate form paired with the sum form. The chosen smaller-coordinate form realizes `min(|u|ᵥ,|w|ᵥ)` independently at each place.

For every `x ∈ normalizedRelations fixedSUnitGroup 2`, the full form product is exactly 1, the retained form product times `H` is exactly 1, and the product of the two locally normalized retained form values is exactly `H⁻³`. This is the needed negative exponent `-2-ε` for projective dimension one with `ε=1`, rather than a renamed finiteness assumption. Here `H` is explicitly the product of the three local sup norms of `(x₀,x₁)`; primes outside the three places contribute 1 for S-unit coordinates, as proved. A standard full rational-height representation and primitive integer normalization/application bridge have not been formalized; only S-unit scaling invariance is claimed, not invariance of the restricted height under arbitrary rational scaling.

## M3.5 elementary classification and unconditional finiteness

Source: [Tijdeman–Wang (1988), Lemma 2, printed p. 179](https://msp.org/pjm/1988/132-1/pjm-v132-n1-p10-s.pdf). The paper attributes the exponential result to L. Hebreus and cites Alex, Lemma 2.1. Both classifications are reconstructed by elementary proofs in `ElementaryThreeTerm.lean`, without invoking the publication as an axiom. The [published correction, pp. 396–398](https://msp.org/pjm/1988/135-2/pjm-v135-n2-p14-s.pdf), was read again: it replaces Lemma 3(b) and the proof of Theorem 3, and does not change Lemma 2. Neither the original false lemma nor its replacement is used. The two publisher PDFs were also opened as primary-source read-only references during this pass; the local source identities remain in `sources.sha256`.

`two_pow_add_one_eq_three_pow_iff` proves exactly `(a,b)=(1,1)` or `(3,2)` for natural exponents. For `a≥3`, reduction modulo 8 forces even `b`; writing `3^b` as a square gives two powers of 2 differing by 2, whose smaller member must be 2 by reduction modulo 4. Small `a` are handled separately. `three_pow_add_one_eq_two_pow_iff` proves exactly `(a,b)=(1,0)` or `(2,1)`; powers of 3 modulo 8 are 1 or 3, forcing `a<3`. Thus exponent zero is covered explicitly, not excluded by an auxiliary positivity assumption.

`Smooth23 n` means every prime divisor of `n` is 2 or 3; `smooth23_factorization` proves the actual product-of-powers representation when `n≠0`. `consecutive_smooth23_classification` proves that a positive `n` with both `n` and `n+1` smooth has `n∈{1,2,3,8}`. Coprimality of consecutive integers excludes a shared 2 or 3, so the nontrivial cases reduce to the two exponential equations.

`exists_primitive_smooth23_triple` extends the already proved primitive pair to `[y₀,y₁,-y₀-y₁]`, with one common fixed-group scaling factor. All three coordinates are nonzero because their rational values are units. Outside-prime norms prove prime support for each absolute value. The primitive pair's Bézout witness gives witnesses for each of the other two pairs too; consequently all coordinate magnitudes are pairwise coprime. Disjoint prime supports among three magnitudes force one magnitude to equal 1. Explicit sign cases for an integer zero sum then make the other two magnitudes consecutive; positivity is asserted only for nonzero absolute values, never for all signed summands.

`primitive_smooth23_bound` proves every magnitude is at most 9. The preceding classification corresponds mathematically to the absolute-value multisets `(1,1,2)`, `(1,2,3)`, `(1,3,4)`, `(1,8,9)`, but no separate explicit-list/permutation theorem is claimed: the checked finiteness proof uses the proved universal bound. `primitive_smooth23_triples_finite` places all allowed signed, ordered triples in `[-9,9]^3`. `fixed_three_term_finite` contains every original normalized relation in the image under `z↦(zᵢ/z₀)`, cancelling the nonzero common scale. This is unconditional finiteness of the complete relation set, independent of any represented integer `n` or analytic-cover hypothesis.

Substantial verification is retained in `verification/m3-5.json` and `verification/m3-5-audit.log`; all failed attempts, verbose logs and the literal-statement challenge stay outside Git in `/tmp/beejsp-m35`. The audit covers all eight public theorems and the literal normalized-relation challenge, with standard foundational axioms only. This is local implementation verification, not a distinct independent review or committed principal reproduction. Mathematical source attribution is preserved; the new Lean formalization was authored locally with Codex assistance. `FixedSUnitFiniteness` still lacks lengths 4–6, `ThreePlaceSubspaceCover` remains unproved with its unchanged full scope, and `jsp_000334` remains absent.

### Checked mathematical correspondence

`FoundationChallenge.lean` reuses the locally authored and previously checked M3.7 ChallengeBC probe, with audit commands removed and no mathematical changes. It derives arbitrary-coefficient normalized homogeneous finiteness from the verified Subspace endpoint, through the actual bounded weighted minimal-block induction. This is an original temporary verification bridge, not copied external analytical implementation. Its hash is in the embedded evidence below. It permits signed integer powers and repeated coordinates, fixes coordinate 0 to 1, has total weighted sum zero, and forbids every proper nonempty weighted subsum. Passing coefficients all 1 reduces to the exact existing predicate.

The new original temporary conversion and principal module is reproduced below. Group equality and set equality are kernel-checked; no normalization or nondegeneracy convention is identified merely by prose. Lengths 2 and 3 reuse `normalized_two_term_finite` and `fixed_three_term_finite`; lengths 4–6 use the proved predicate equality and external-environment finiteness. No conditional theorem replaces the principal claim.

```lean
import ElementaryThreeTerm
import FoundationChallenge

namespace JSP000334
open Erdos407.SubspaceApplication
open scoped BigOperators

theorem external_group_eq_fixed : U23.group = fixedSUnitGroup := by
  rw [FoundationChallenge.signed_group_is_generated]
  congr 1
  change ({Units.mk0 (-1) (by norm_num), Units.mk0 2 (by norm_num),
    Units.mk0 3 (by norm_num)} : Set ℚˣ) = {-1, twoUnit, threeUnit}
  have hm : Units.mk0 (-1 : ℚ) (by norm_num) = (-1 : ℚˣ) := by
    apply Units.ext
    rfl
  rw [hm]
  rfl

theorem fixed_coordinate_iff (q : ℚ) :
    (∃ u : fixedSUnitGroup, (u : ℚˣ).val = q) ↔ Erdos407.PadicProduct.IsUnit23 q := by
  rw [← external_group_eq_fixed]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨u, rfl⟩
    exact u.property
  · intro h
    exact ⟨U23.ofIsUnit23 q h, U23.coe_ofIsUnit23 q h⟩

theorem normalized_predicates_eq (n : ℕ) :
    normalizedRelations fixedSUnitGroup n =
      FoundationChallenge.rationalNormalized (n := n) (fun _ => 1) := by
  ext x
  simp only [normalizedRelations, FoundationChallenge.rationalNormalized,
    Set.mem_setOf_eq, fixed_coordinate_iff, one_mul, Nondegenerate]

theorem fixed_normalized_finite {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 5) :
    (normalizedRelations fixedSUnitGroup n).Finite := by
  rw [normalized_predicates_eq]
  exact FoundationChallenge.rational_normalized_finite hn _ (by intro i; norm_num)

theorem fixed_sunit_finiteness : FixedSUnitFiniteness := by
  intro m
  fin_cases m
  · exact normalized_two_term_finite fixedSUnitGroup
  · exact fixed_three_term_finite
  · exact fixed_normalized_finite (by decide)
  · exact fixed_normalized_finite (by decide)
  · exact fixed_normalized_finite (by decide)

theorem jsp_000334 : NewmanConjecture := by
  exact newman_of_fixed_sunit_finiteness fixed_sunit_finiteness

end JSP000334
```

Mathematical source: EGST88 §4, printed pp. 122–124, especially (4.3)–(4.6) and the following induction; Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.1 at p. 118. The primitive reduction clears only the first three coordinates, using normalization x₀=1 and the common denominator of x₁,x₂. Its first coordinate is D; dividing the total gcd yields a Bézout-primitive triple. The gcd's support is bounded because it divides D, not because coordinate pairs are coprime. An actual S-unit quotient realizes this scaling, and the eliminated fourth coordinate retains the same factor. `exists_primitive_four_term_relation` proves all four integer coordinates are nonzero, sum to zero, retain `Nondegenerate`, and scale the original x exactly. Shared primes, negative coordinates and repeated values are not excluded. Neither the bound 9 nor the three-term pairwise-coprime classification is assumed for the four-term tuple.

The three coordinate/sum forms are rational linear maps. Independence is proved by the standard basis calculation for each omission, with determinant-equivalent rank 3. Maximal-coordinate choice is made independently at infinity, 2 and 3; the finite pattern type has cardinal 27. For each primitive triple, Bézout prevents every coordinate being divisible by any prime, giving a finite-prime maximum of exactly 1 and exact primitive Archimedean height. The S-unit product formula and fourth-coordinate elimination give retained product times height = 1 and normalized product H⁻⁴, with H≥1. The normalization exponent is for three forms / P² and ε=1. This is application arithmetic, not a proof of the finite-subspace conclusion after EGST88 (4.6).

### Original mathematical sources and proof gap

EGST88 §4, printed pp.122–124, states (4.1), cites Schlickewei [69] for full places, applies it after (4.6), and performs the weighted induction at p.124. The exact cited publication is *The p-adic Thue-Siegel-Roth-Schmidt theorem*, Arch. Math. 29 (1977), 267–270, [publisher DOI page](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01220404). Direct PDF retrieval returned HTML subscription-preview content, not the original proof; no internal theorem number is asserted for that unread body.

An original sufficient finite-cover theorem and its reduction proof were actually located: H.P. Schlickewei, *On products of special linear forms with algebraic coefficients*, Acta Arith. 31 (1976), 389–398, DOI 10.4064/aa-31-4-389-398, [original scan](https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa31/aa3148.pdf). Theorem 4.1 is on printed p.395 and its proof on p.396. The six landscape PDF sheets include adjacent unrelated pp.388 and 399, excluded from this paper's evidence. Specialize n=3, t=2, distinct primes 2/3, all three independent forms at each place, epsilon=1 and rational coefficients. Primitivity excludes zero; our supremum height is the source norm; product times height ≤1 is exactly product ≤H⁻¹. Proper rational subspaces can be enlarged to proper hyperplanes. Zero evaluations already lie in finitely many form kernels. This suffices for every one of the existing 27 patterns and preserves the entire primitive domain and inequality.

The reduction proof explicitly invokes Satz 2.1 of *Linearformen mit algebraischen Koeffizienten*, Manuscripta Math. 18 (1976), 147–185, and Schmidt's *Norm form equations*, Ann. Math. 96 (1972), pp.535–537, for finite-subspace extraction. The Acta paper's p.391 also locates the weak-general p-adic Roth-system criterion at Manuscripta Satz 1.2, proof §7. These delegated full proof bodies were not obtained/audited. [EuDML record](https://eudml.org/doc/154385) access timed out in the browser and returned HTTP 403 in the direct retrieval. This identifies missing source material precisely; it does not show that no lawful accessible copy exists. The complete analytic prerequisite inventory and specialization cannot be certified from the reduction proof alone.

The six supplied sources are insufficient for a self-contained analytic foundation: EGST88 sketches the application, Tijdeman–Wang Lemma 6 at p.190 refers to Evertse/van der Poorten–Schlickewei, and the published correction repairs Lemma 3(b)/Theorem 3. Bajpai–Bennett's preprint/published text and the thesis use external complex/p-adic logarithmic bounds and existing S-unit finiteness. Their quantitative alternative has not been validated as a shorter independent route. Neither a citation nor their source theorem statements are formal proofs of the missing cover.
